text.p: STOCKS GOLD
Dow Jones close Latest spot rate
FTSE-100 close CRUDE OIL
Nikkei-225 latest $23.75 per bbl
Blue-chip stocks edged higher Friday after swinging wildly amid the so-called triple-witching expirations of December futures and options.
Bonds fell, and the dollar was mixed in quiet trading as traders looked to lock in profits before the upcoming Christmas and New Year's holidays.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 10.76 points to 6,484.40. In early trading, the Dow rose 75 points to 6,548.99, putting it a shade above its record close of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25.
For the week, the Dow was up 179.53, its strongest week since the first full week of November, when blue chips began a scorching month-long rally of more than 500 points.

In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,535 to 968 on very heavy volume of 650 million shares on the NYSE, the third largest total in history and the highest since July 16, when the exchange handled a record 680.3 million shares in volume.
"Today's action and volatility was directly related to options expiration," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Even so, analysts said they doubted the market would make much headway next week although individual sectors could see action.

"We'll probably see some more rotation going into the end of the year but we're not going to see much new money," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "I just think there's not a lot of demand for new stock going into next week."

In contrast to Thursday's session, when a powerhouse rally sent the Dow up 126.87 points for its second biggest point gain ever, the market appeared decidedly cautious, despite an opening blitz of activity in blue-chip stocks.
The trading volume on the NYSE was boosted by the triple-witching expiration of stock options, index options and futures, which triggered huge position-squaring by institutions.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell one-qaurter point, or $2.50 per $1,000 face value, raising its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.61 percent from 6.59 percent at Thursday's close.
The dollar fell to 1.5515 German marks from 1.5575 late Thursday, but edged up to 114.27 Japanese yen from 114.03 yen.
Oil and grain prices fell as traders took profits on this week's gains as sentiment improved about the availability of supplies.
Heating oil for January delivery lost 0.81 cent to settle at 72.97 cents a gallon, and January gasoline closed 1.03 cents lower at 70.19 cents a gallon.
Crude oil prices also fell, with February crude down 37 cents a barrel at $25.08 in sympathy with heating oil and on bearish supply news of its own, traders said.

At the Chicago Board of Trade, wheat futures closed lower on improved weather in that country's wheat growing regions. The Argentine crop has been hurt this year by torrential rains. March wheat ended at $3.93-1/4 per bushel, down 7 cents.

Overseas, London's FTSE index ended 26.3 points higher at 4,077.6, rising 105.2 from last Friday. In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average closed up 119.79 points, or 0.61 percent, at 19,690.46, a drop of 650.93 from last Friday.
